title: Guy Named ‘Quantrivious’ And 11 Co-Conspirators Busted For $250,000 Chicken Heist
text:
Image not from story(Photo by Brad Vest/Getty Images)

A crew of criminals got caught red-handed hauling a quarter-million dollars in stolen chicken out of a big rig behind a roadside motel.

Federal agents rounded up the group in Memphis, according to a release from the U.S. Marshals Service. A task force made the arrests Tuesday while serving an aggravated robbery warrant on 33-year-old Javunte Johnson.

Officers found Johnson and a dozen others pulling pallets of poultry, worth $250,000, off an 18-wheeler parked behind a motel, WMC Action News 5 reported. The group scattered, but agents chased down every one of them. (RELATED: Pizza Parlor Owner Says Memphis Is Safer Without National Guard, Refuses To Serve Them)

What started as a warrant sweep turned up far more than frozen birds. Detectives seized three handguns, roughly $110,000 in other stolen goods, and a stash of fentanyl and cocaine, WMC reported. Investigators concluded the merchandise coming off the truck had all been stolen.

Memphis Safe Task Force Arrests 13 People Trying to Steal $250K Worth of Chicken from a Semi-Trailer#USMarshals https://t.co/Bpp4qhjbW8

Among those hauled in was 25-year-old Quantrivious Shavers, who now faces a theft count, a felon-in-possession charge, and a fentanyl distribution charge, according to Memphis police cited by WMC. Jessie Moore, 37, also caught a felon-in-possession charge. Johnson drew the heaviest slate, including the aggravated robbery count that launched the operation.

Police charged 12 people in the bust. The theft counts, covering property valued between $60,000 and $250,000, landed on Johnson, Shavers, Robert Wilson, 56, Samuel Jackson, 38, John Shipp, 47, Rico Jackson, 36, Devean Hoyle, 45, Trashawn Featherson, 35, Robert Dishmon, 40, and Marcellous McKinney, 38. Wilson and McKinney also caught evading arrest counts, while Moore and 21-year-old Alexis Pike were charged with fleeing on foot. Jackson faces a cocaine distribution count.

The chicken caper was part of a busy day for the task force, which logged 49 arrests total that Tuesday, the Marshals said. President Donald Trump created the multi-agency unit through a memorandum signed in Sept. 2025. The unit pulls in federal, state and local officers alongside Tennessee National Guard members.

Marshals say the operation has produced 12,796 arrests and seized 2,163 illegal guns since it began.
